articles.title: Coalitions Make the Left Stronger
articles.author: Midwestern Socialist -- Chicago DSA
articles.content_excerpt: DSA has had a string of spectacular electoral victories. With success comes greater media attention, growing membership, and new challenges. One of the most important questions is how to build broad unity that can achieve transformative policies. And how do we criticize each other and political allies without falling into sectarian purism where differences overshadow what we hold in common and disrupt working together? The specter haunting DSA seems to be the possibility of socialist congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (AOC) joining the presidential primary. articles.title: Under Israeli Settler Attacks, I Feel I Am Not Alive
articles.author: Miriame Mazid
articles.content_excerpt: In the West Bank village of At-Tuwani this July 19, Ruqayya Rabe’i, three months pregnant, lay in her room beside her four sleeping daughters. At 12:30 a.m., the first stones hit her home. She rushed to check the front door. There in the living room, she found her fifteen-year-old son, Usayd, sleeping directly below a window where, according to Ruqayya, several settlers were armed with guns and knives and trying to force their way in. She tried to shake her son awake, but he didn’t stir. When the settlers noticed her, she fled, certain that if they saw him, they would shoot. The window was shattered, a chemical compound poured through it, and the frame went up in flames, Ruqayya said. articles.title: Will AI Destroy the Meritocracy?
articles.author: Matt Bruenig
articles.content_excerpt: There is a lot of debate about whether artificial intelligence, large language models (LLMs) in particular, will make people smarter or dumber. The case for dumber is that LLMs can be used as a substitute for learning. Rather than struggling through a subject and working your brain around understanding it, you can just have an LLM produce the desired output. The case for smarter is that LLMs can be used like a very patient tutor who answers your questions and thereby helps you understand and learn things. Generally speaking, I think the answer is obviously both. This is true even for a particular individual who may use AI to help them understand certain things better while also using it to help them avoid learning other things. This tracks my own experience. articles.title: Spiking Bond Yields Pay the Rich and Squeeze Everyone Else
articles.author: Matías Vernengo
articles.content_excerpt: The recent rise in long-term US Treasury yields has revived a familiar story about fiscal irresponsibility. Commentators point to large federal deficits, growing public debt, and the volume of Treasury securities coming onto the market. From this perspective, higher yields are the market’s response to excessive government borrowing, and the Trump administration’s policy amounts to fiscal recklessness. This interpretation rests on an old and misleading conception of financial markets. It treats government and private borrowers as competing for a limited pool of savings, so that larger deficits necessarily drive interest rates upward. articles.title: How Domestic Workers built POWER in Philadelphia - The Forge
articles.content_excerpt: A few years ago, one of our members — a Black Caribbean immigrant nanny working in one of Philadelphia’s wealthiest neighborhoods — asked her employer for a written contract. She had that right under the city’s Domestic Worker Bill of Rights, which domestic workers won in 2019. Instead, she was fired on the spot. After that, she was quietly blacklisted in the neighborhood’s parent Facebook groups, a form of retaliation that could itself be deemed illegal in many labor violation cases. I’ve spent years working as an organizer alongside Philadelphia nannies, caregivers, and housecleaners to win critical labor protections and the dignity and respect all workers deserve. articles.title: The Left Can’t Win Without an Internationalist Vision
articles.author: Pine and Roses -- Maine DSA
articles.content_excerpt: As we enter a new age of imperial wars, internationalism is very much back on the Left’s agenda. But what is internationalism? And why does it matter? The Left’s preoccupation with “internationalism” stems from the fact that its political project has always been tied in some way to what might be called universal emancipation. To emancipate is to free someone or something from a power, and universal emancipation stands for the liberation of everyone from all domination. The aim of the Left, in other words, is not simply to redistribute wealth, expand state services, or roll back racial discrimination in one’s own country; it is to abolish every form of oppression and domination everywhere. By definition, universal emancipation has to be global or not at all. A World of States But the globe

articles.author: San Francisco DSA
articles.content_excerpt: DSA San Francisco stands in strong opposition to Mayor Lurie’s three proposed charter amendments for November 2026 which seek to limit San Franciscans’ ability to place measures on the ballot, reduce democratic oversight over city spending, and further centralize power under the Mayor. The measures are funded by a set of tech and real estate capitalists, to the tune of $8.6 million so far . All of these measures undermine the working class’ ability to govern ourselves and hold our officials accountable for their decisions while cynically being marketed as an effort to “clean up City Hall,” despite most of San Francisco’s recent corruption emanating from the Mayor’s Office. articles.title: Centrist Democrats Are Trying to Throw the Michigan Race
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: In Michigan, where progressive Abdul El-Sayed is facing off for the must-win Senate seat against Donald Trump–backed Mike Rogers, Democrats have a problem. How to reconcile their distaste for their own party’s nominee with the imperative to care about winning? Attorney General Dana Nessel modeled a way out of the bind with a comically backhanded endorsement. Tasked with trying to convince Jewish Democrats that they should vote for El-Sayed despite the blizzard of smears charging he’s a dangerous antisemite, Attorney General Dana Nessel offered the most unappetizing of unappetizing pitches.
